characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.description: A sharp-witted investigator who interrupts Watson, deeply analyzes a newly received envelope and paper, and views Professor Moriarty as a mastermind.

characters.name: Watson
characters.description: The narrator and a doctor who gets annoyed by Holmes's sardonic tone and publicly labels Moriarty a criminal.

characters.name: Professor Moriarty
characters.description: A celebrated professor and author of a mathematical treatise who secretly operates as the master schemer and controlling brain of the underworld.

characters.name: Moriarty
characters.description: A professor, celebrated author of 'The Dynamics of an Asteroid', and mastermind of the underworld.

characters.name: Porlock
characters.description: An individual whose handwriting is recognized by the speaker through a distinctive Greek 'e'.

characters.name: Holmes
characters.description: A detective who receives advance information about crimes from Porlock and analyzes encoded messages.

locations.name: This great city
locations.description: A city with teeming millions where Porlock claimed he could not be traced.

relationships.subject: Watson
relationships.explanation: Watson sits at the breakfast table with Holmes, engaged in conversation.

relationships.subject: Sherlock Holmes
relationships.explanation: Holmes regards Moriarty as the greatest criminal schemer of all time and expects a future reckoning with him.

relationships.subject: Porlock
relationships.explanation: Porlock is described as being in touch with the formidable and sinister Professor Moriarty.

relationships.subject: Watson
relationships.explanation: Watson is listening to and discussing Porlock with the speaker.

relationships.subject: Porlock
relationships.explanation: Porlock has occasionally provided Holmes with advance information that helps prevent crimes.

relationships.subject: Holmes
relationships.explanation: Holmes sends an occasional ten-pound note to Porlock by devious methods to encourage him.

relationships.subject: Watson
relationships.explanation: Watson listens to Holmes's explanation and leans over him to examine a document.

relationships.subject: Professor Moriarty
relationships.explanation: Holmes notes that members of that party refer to Professor Moriarty as the predominant 'He'.
